celebration-plaza-amphitheater.name: Celebration Plaza Amphitheater
celebration-plaza-amphitheater.description: A natural outdoor amphitheater on the east bank of the White River at the west end of Celebration Plaza, with tiered limestone seating and a private waterfall.
celebration-plaza-amphitheater.hours: Open daily 5:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. as part of White River State Park. Rentals, programs, private events and temporary park alerts can close or control access independently.
celebration-plaza-amphitheater.location: The amphitheater is tucked into the hillside on the east bank of the White River at the west end of Celebration Plaza. The pin is the reviewed OpenStreetMap point for the named Celebration Plaza and Amphitheater feature.
celebration-plaza-amphitheater.parking: Use the White River State Park underground garage or another downtown parking option, then approach through Celebration Plaza. The operator currently lists garage rates beginning at $10 for up to two hours and warns that special-event rates can differ.
celebration-plaza-amphitheater.restrooms: The operator does not identify a dedicated amphitheater restroom on the venue or park-map pages. Plan around restrooms inside nearby staffed attractions during their own hours, and confirm event facilities when access is important.
celebration-plaza-amphitheater.fees: The operator lists no general admission charge for ordinary access to this outdoor park space. Reserved, private or ticketed events can restrict entry or charge separately; garage parking is paid.
celebration-plaza-amphitheater.accessibility: The venue is built into a hillside with tiered limestone seating. The operator does not publish a route-by-route step-free access description, so visitors who need a specific entrance or seating route should contact park staff before arrival.
celebration-plaza-amphitheater.dogs: White River State Park prohibits animals off leash and leashes longer than six feet. Events may impose additional animal restrictions, so check the listing or signs before entering an event setup.
celebration-plaza-amphitheater.family: The outdoor setting can support a short park stop, but children need close supervision around the waterfall, tiered stone seating and any event equipment or restricted areas.
celebration-plaza-amphitheater.need: Check the current park alert and events pages on the day of the visit. The visit page still displays an August 15 closure notice that explicitly says the space reopened August 16, so that notice is expired rather than evidence of a current closure.
celebration-plaza-amphitheater.imageAlt: Celebration Plaza Amphitheater beside the canal headwaters and lawn at White River State Park

canal-walk.name: Canal Walk
canal-walk.description: A three-mile waterside loop along the Central Canal from White River State Park to 11th Street for walkers, runners, bicyclists and sightseers.
canal-walk.hours: Open daily 5:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m. The route can be affected by park alerts, events, maintenance and weather even when the ordinary grounds schedule applies.
canal-walk.location: The Canal Walk runs from the White River through White River State Park to West Street and then north toward 10th and 11th streets. This pin marks the reviewed named paved Canal Walk segment inside White River State Park; it is an arrival point for the route, not the center of the full loop.
canal-walk.parking: For this White River State Park access, use the park's underground garage or another downtown parking option and join the Canal Walk inside the park. The operator currently lists garage rates beginning at $10 for up to two hours and says special-event rates can differ.
canal-walk.restrooms: The operator does not identify a dedicated public restroom on this Canal Walk segment. Plan around restrooms inside staffed park attractions during their own hours rather than assuming continuous restroom access along the three-mile loop.
canal-walk.fees: The operator lists no general admission charge for ordinary Canal Walk use. Parking, rentals, gondolas, attractions, restaurants and special events charge separately.
canal-walk.accessibility: The pinned named segment is mapped as a paved footway, but the operator does not publish a route-by-route accessibility guarantee for the entire three-mile loop. Confirm current detours, grades and any needed accommodation before relying on a continuous route.
canal-walk.dogs: White River State Park prohibits animals off leash and leashes longer than six feet. Keep dogs controlled around other walkers, runners and bicyclists, and follow any event-specific restrictions.
canal-walk.family: The waterside route can work for a family walk, but adults should supervise children beside the canal and around shared-path traffic. Choose a turnaround distance instead of assuming every group should complete the full loop.
canal-walk.need: This is a linear route, not a single point: the pin marks the White River State Park segment. Check same-day park alerts and events for detours or closures, and remember that rentals and nearby attractions keep separate schedules.
canal-walk.imageAlt: Canal Walk paths and water along the Central Canal in downtown Indianapolis

eagle-creek-ornithology-center.name: Eagle Creek Park Ornithology Center
eagle-creek-ornithology-center.description: The Eagle Creek Park Ornithology Center is a staffed bird-focused nature center with exhibits, wildlife observation areas, educational programs and non-releasable raptor ambassadors.
eagle-creek-ornithology-center.hours: Closed Monday; open Tuesday-Saturday 10:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. and Sunday 1:00-5:00 p.m. Programs and aviary access can change independently, and park gates close on their seasonal schedule.
eagle-creek-ornithology-center.location: The center is at 6515 Delong Road in the northern part of Eagle Creek Park. The exact pin uses the Commons photograph's camera geotag, which depicts this exterior and matches the official facility address.
eagle-creek-ornithology-center.parking: Use the 71st Street park entrance at 7100 North Eagle Creek Parkway, then follow the park map toward 6515 Delong Road and the Ornithology Center lot. Park admission is collected at the gate.
eagle-creek-ornithology-center.restrooms: The staffed center is the reliable restroom location during building hours. Do not assume indoor restroom access before opening, after closing or during an unplanned facility closure.
eagle-creek-ornithology-center.fees: Center admission is free with paid Eagle Creek Park admission. Special programs, group bookings and other park activities may charge separately.
eagle-creek-ornithology-center.accessibility: The official center page welcomes people of all ages and abilities and identifies indoor exhibits and wildlife observation areas. Visitors with route-specific needs should call ahead because trails, outdoor viewing areas and temporary closures can vary.
eagle-creek-ornithology-center.dogs: Dogs must remain leashed in Eagle Creek Park, but the center and raptor areas are wildlife-focused facilities. Leave pets outside the building and aviary unless staff or posted rules explicitly allow an accommodation.
eagle-creek-ornithology-center.family: The exhibits, observation areas and raptor ambassadors are designed for varied ages. Groups of 20 or more should call ahead, and children must follow staff rules around live animals.
eagle-creek-ornithology-center.need: The Commons file is titled as a nature center but its description identifies the building as the Ornithology Center. Weekly program times are not a substitute for checking the current calendar; arrive before the building's posted closing time.
eagle-creek-ornithology-center.imageAlt: Snow-covered stone exterior of the Eagle Creek Park Ornithology Center among mature trees

garfield-park-conservatory.name: Garfield Park Conservatory
garfield-park-conservatory.description: A staffed tropical conservatory at Garfield Park with plant displays and a koi pond, operating on a shorter schedule than the surrounding park.
garfield-park-conservatory.hours: Closed Monday; open Tuesday-Saturday 10:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. and Sunday 1:00-5:00 p.m. Last admission is 4:45 p.m.; closures and events can change access.
garfield-park-conservatory.location: The Conservatory is at 2505 Conservatory Drive on the east side of the Sunken Garden. The pin is the reviewed OpenStreetMap point for the named building.
garfield-park-conservatory.parking: Navigate to 2505 Conservatory Drive and use the developed parking nearest the Conservatory and garden complex. Do not use the general Pagoda Drive pin when building hours matter.
garfield-park-conservatory.restrooms: Indoor restroom access is tied to staffed Conservatory hours. Do not assume the building or its facilities will be open before 10:00 a.m., after the last admission, on Monday or during a closure.
garfield-park-conservatory.fees: Admission is $4 per person. Special events and programs may have separate pricing, so verify the event listing before arriving.
garfield-park-conservatory.accessibility: The Conservatory is a developed indoor visitor facility, but the operator does not publish a route-by-route accessibility guarantee on this page. Contact staff before relying on a specific entrance, mobility accommodation or sensory condition.
garfield-park-conservatory.dogs: Outdoor park rules require dogs to remain leashed, but the Conservatory is an indoor planted exhibit. Confirm service-animal and pet access with staff rather than assuming the general park dog rule permits indoor entry.
garfield-park-conservatory.family: The plant displays and koi pond can suit varied ages. Children should remain supervised around water and displays, and groups should confirm current program or reservation requirements.
garfield-park-conservatory.need: Arrive before the 4:45 p.m. last admission. The neighboring Sunken Garden is a separate, free destination with the same weekly schedule but may close for inclement weather.
garfield-park-conservatory.imageAlt: Orange and white koi swimming in the Garfield Park Conservatory pond

sunken-garden.name: Sunken Garden
sunken-garden.description: The formal Sunken Garden beside Garfield Park Conservatory, with seasonal plantings, walkways and restored fountains.
sunken-garden.hours: Closed Monday; open Tuesday-Saturday 10:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. and Sunday 1:00-5:00 p.m. The garden closes in inclement weather.
sunken-garden.location: The garden is immediately west of the Conservatory at the 2505 Conservatory Drive complex. The exact pin is the reviewed named garden point, corroborated by Commons camera geotags.
sunken-garden.parking: Navigate to 2505 Conservatory Drive and use parking for the Conservatory and garden complex. The garden and Conservatory share an arrival area but keep separate admission rules.
sunken-garden.restrooms: The most reliable nearby restrooms are inside staffed facilities during their posted hours. Do not assume indoor access when the garden is closed or after the Conservatory's last admission.
sunken-garden.fees: The Sunken Garden is free. The adjacent Conservatory charges $4 per person, and events or programs may be priced separately.
sunken-garden.accessibility: The formal garden uses developed walks, but grades, route conditions and temporary closures can affect access. Contact the facility before relying on a specific step-free path.
sunken-garden.dogs: Dogs in the outdoor park must remain leashed, but planted garden areas may post additional restrictions. Keep animals controlled and out of beds and fountains, and follow signs on arrival.
sunken-garden.family: The garden offers a short outdoor visit, but children need supervision around fountains, steps and plantings. Weather can close the garden independently of nearby buildings.
sunken-garden.need: The restored fountains reopened June 6, 2026. Fountain operation and garden access remain weather- and maintenance-dependent, so verify current notices before traveling specifically for the water display.
sunken-garden.imageAlt: Restored fountains, flower planters and formal lawns in Garfield Park's Sunken Garden

garfield-park-arts-center.name: Garfield Park Arts Center
garfield-park-arts-center.description: A community arts facility in Garfield Park with galleries, classes and programs in a renovated historic building.
garfield-park-arts-center.hours: Closed Sunday and Monday; open Tuesday-Saturday 10:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. by appointment. Program and event times may differ, so confirm before visiting.
garfield-park-arts-center.location: The Arts Center is at 2432 Conservatory Drive, west of the Conservatory and Sunken Garden. The pin is the reviewed OpenStreetMap building centroid.
garfield-park-arts-center.parking: Navigate to 2432 Conservatory Drive and use parking serving the Arts Center. It is a different building from the Conservatory, so do not rely on the garden pin for a timed appointment.
garfield-park-arts-center.restrooms: Indoor restrooms are available only when the Arts Center is open for an appointment, program or event. Confirm access before planning around the facility.
garfield-park-arts-center.fees: The facility page does not post a general gallery admission charge. Classes, workshops, rentals and special events may have fees; verify the selected activity.
garfield-park-arts-center.accessibility: The Arts Center is a developed public building, but the facility page does not document every route or accommodation. Contact staff when a specific entrance, seating or program accommodation is needed.
garfield-park-arts-center.dogs: Outdoor park rules require leashes, but this is an indoor arts facility. Confirm service-animal and pet access with staff rather than assuming ordinary pets may enter.
garfield-park-arts-center.family: Classes, galleries and programs serve different ages and may require registration. Confirm the program description and appointment before bringing children.
garfield-park-arts-center.need: The posted schedule is by appointment, not guaranteed walk-in access. Check the current calendar or contact the Arts Center before making a destination-specific trip.
garfield-park-arts-center.imageAlt: Eastern exterior and colorful entrance of the Garfield Park Arts Center

holliday-park-ruins.name: Holliday Park Ruins
holliday-park-ruins.description: The landmark Ruins combine sculptural remnants from New York's demolished St. Paul Building with gardens and an outdoor plaza in Holliday Park.
holliday-park-ruins.hours: The Ruins are outdoors within park grounds, which are open dawn to dusk. Events, maintenance and weather can limit portions of the plaza independently.
holliday-park-ruins.location: Enter Holliday Park from Spring Mill Road and turn left from the south gate toward the Ruins. The exact pin is the reviewed OpenStreetMap Ruins point.
holliday-park-ruins.parking: Use the free lot west of the Ruins. The playground and Nature Center have separate lots, so select the Ruins pin before entering the park.
holliday-park-ruins.restrooms: The Holliday Park Foundation reports maintained restrooms and drinking fountains near the Ruins. Availability can vary with maintenance, events and cold weather; the Nature Center is the staffed fallback during its hours.
holliday-park-ruins.fees: The operator does not post an admission fee for ordinary visits to the Ruins, and park parking is free. Reserved events and programs may charge separately.
holliday-park-ruins.accessibility: The revitalized Ruins plaza has developed approaches, but routes, surfaces and event setups can change. Contact the park for a specific step-free route or accommodation.
holliday-park-ruins.dogs: Dogs in Holliday Park must remain leashed. Keep pets controlled around gardens, masonry, events and other visitors, and follow any plaza-specific signs.
holliday-park-ruins.family: The Ruins are an outdoor art and history destination, not a play structure. Supervise children around masonry, fountains, stairs and event equipment.
holliday-park-ruins.need: The structure is an outdoor installation built from preserved facade elements and reopened after revitalization in 2016. Do not treat it as an enterable historic building; check the event calendar for temporary restrictions.
holliday-park-ruins.imageAlt: Brick, stone columns and carved figures of the Holliday Park Ruins surrounded by summer gardens

holliday-park-nature-center.name: Holliday Park Nature Center
holliday-park-nature-center.description: A staffed environmental education center featuring Habitat Hall exhibits and nature programming within Holliday Park.
holliday-park-nature-center.hours: Open Monday-Saturday 9:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. The building is not listed as open Sunday; programs, holidays and unplanned closures can change access.
holliday-park-nature-center.location: The Nature Center is inside Holliday Park at 6363 Spring Mill Road. The pin uses the reviewed OpenStreetMap building centroid rather than the inaccurate camera location embedded in one interior photograph.
holliday-park-nature-center.parking: Use the free lot near the Nature Center. The Ruins and playground have separate lots, so follow signs for the staffed building after entering from Spring Mill Road.
holliday-park-nature-center.restrooms: The staffed Nature Center is the park's most reliable restroom location during building hours. Do not assume indoor access on Sunday, before 9:00 a.m., after 5:00 p.m. or during a closure.
holliday-park-nature-center.fees: The operator does not post general admission for ordinary Nature Center and Habitat Hall visits, and parking is free. Programs, camps, rentals and special events may charge.
holliday-park-nature-center.accessibility: The Nature Center is a developed indoor visitor facility, but the operator does not publish a route-by-route guarantee on this page. Contact staff before relying on a specific mobility, sensory or program accommodation.
holliday-park-nature-center.dogs: Outdoor park rules require leashes, but the Nature Center is an indoor wildlife-education facility. Confirm service-animal and pet access with staff rather than assuming ordinary pets may enter.
holliday-park-nature-center.family: Habitat Hall's interactive exhibits and nature programming are intended for varied ages. Check the calendar for program registration and supervise children around exhibits.
holliday-park-nature-center.need: Building hours are shorter than dawn-to-dusk park hours. The destination image shows an exact Habitat Hall exhibit, but its embedded camera GPS is inconsistent with the official address and was not used for navigation.
holliday-park-nature-center.imageAlt: Interactive Cricket Frog Call exhibit inside Habitat Hall at the Holliday Park Nature Center
